summary.en: **My, your, his, her…** go before a noun and agree with the **owner**, not with the thing: _Sara loves her job_, _Tom loves his job_. **Mine, yours, hers…** stand alone: _That coat is mine._ Use **'s** for people and **of** for things: _my manager's office_, _the end of the film_. **Myself, themselves…** are used only when the subject and object are the same person; English also uses **my** (not _the_) with body parts and clothes.
summary.es: My/his/her concuerdan con el poseedor, no con la cosa. Y no uses el artículo con partes del cuerpo: «me lavo las manos» = I wash my hands. Muchos verbos reflexivos en español (levantarse, ducharse) no llevan reflexivo en inglés.

form: Determiners: **my, your, his, her, its, our, their** + noun (no article before them)
Pronouns: **mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs** (no noun after them)
**'s** with people: _Ana's brother_, _my parents' house_; **of** with things: _the door of the car_
**a friend of mine / yours / his** (one of several friends)
Reflexives: **myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves**

uses.text: **Possession** → determiner or 's: _Where is your passport?_ _That's Clara's laptop._
**Without a noun** → mine, yours…: _Is this pen yours?_ _No, mine is blue._
**Subject = object** → reflexive: _She taught herself Italian._ _We enjoyed ourselves._

note.en: Compare _They hurt themselves_ (each one hurt himself) with _They hurt each other_ (A hurt B and B hurt A).
note.es: Themselves = cada uno a sí mismo; each other = el uno al otro.

uses.text: **Emphasis** → reflexive after the noun: _The director herself answered the phone._ _I did it myself._ **By myself** = alone.
**Body parts and clothes** → possessive: _He broke his arm._ _Put your coat on._

mistakes.wrong: Sara forgot his umbrella at the office.
mistakes.right: Sara forgot her umbrella at the office.

why.en: The possessive agrees with the owner (Sara = her), not with the object.
why.es: Concuerda con el poseedor: Sara → her; no con el paparaguas.

mistakes.wrong: I washed the hands and brushed the teeth.
mistakes.right: I washed my hands and brushed my teeth.

why.en: Use a possessive with body parts, not the.
why.es: Con partes del cuerpo se usa my/your…, no the.

mistakes.wrong: A colleague of me recommended this book.
mistakes.right: A colleague of mine recommended this book.

why.en: After of, use the possessive pronoun (mine), not the object pronoun.
why.es: «Un compañero mío» = a colleague of mine.

mistakes.wrong: I feel myself tired, so I will relax myself at home.
mistakes.right: I feel tired, so I will relax at home.

why.en: Many verbs that are reflexive in Spanish are not reflexive in English: get up, wash, shave, relax, feel.
why.es: Levantarse, ducharse, afeitarse, relajarse, sentirse: sin reflexivo en inglés.

mistakes.wrong: The car of my father is in the garage.
mistakes.right: My father's car is in the garage.

why.en: With people, 's is usual: the owner comes first, then 's, then the thing.
why.es: «El coche de mi padre» = my father's car; no se invierte con of.

examples.en: My manager has asked me to rewrite my report by Friday.
examples.es: Mi jefa me ha pedido que reescriba mi informe para el viernes.

examples.en: I'm not sure whose keys these are. Are they yours?
examples.es: No sé de quién son estas llaves. ¿Son tuyas?

examples.en: The company has changed its name twice in five years.
Our neighbours' dog barks all night.
She taught herself to code during lockdown.
You can't blame anyone but yourself.
They've known each other since secondary school.
He cut himself while he was chopping onions.
Can I borrow your charger? Mine has stopped working.
I'd rather do it myself than wait for someone else.

practice.prompt: Sara forgot ___ umbrella, so she got soaked.

explanation.en: The possessive agrees with the owner, Sara, who is a woman: her.

practice.prompt: Don't worry about us. We can look after ___.

explanation.en: Subject and object are the same people (we), so we use ourselves.

practice.prompt: Tom and Ana have known ___ since university.

explanation.en: Each knows the other: a reciprocal action takes each other.
There is no noun after the gap, so we need the pronoun mine.
Body parts take a possessive determiner, not the.
